name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q01 - Anther structure, microsporangium layers, and microsporogenesis

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding the stamen, microsporangium, and microsporogenesis in angiosperms:

Statement I: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, dithecous, and tetragonal, containing four microsporangia located at the corners.

Statement II: The innermost wall layer of the microsporangium, the tapetum, nourishes developing pollen grains and its cells typically possess dense cytoplasm with more than one nucleus.

Statement III: Each cell of the sporogenous tissue is a potential pollen mother cell that undergoes mitosis to form a haploid microspore tetrad.

Statement IV: Pollen grains are generally spherical and measure about 25–50 micrometers in diameter.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In flowering plants, the male reproductive unit (stamen) produces pollen grains inside microsporangia through meiotic division of sporogenous cells, supported by specialised anther wall layers.

Step 2: Evaluation of Anther Morphology and Tapetum
A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with two thecae per lobe (dithecous) and appears four-sided (tetragonal) in transverse section, bearing four microsporangia at the corners. Surrounding each microsporangium are the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and the innermost tapetum. Tapetal cells have dense cytoplasm and generally more than one nucleus, serving to nourish developing pollen grains. Thus, both the description of anther organisation and the description of the tapetum are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Microsporogenesis and Pollen Size
Each cell of the sporogenous tissue is a potential pollen mother cell (PMC), but microspore tetrads are formed from PMCs through meiosis (reduction division), not mitosis, so that the resulting microspores are haploid. Therefore, the claim that PMCs undergo mitosis to form tetrads is incorrect. Meanwhile, typical pollen grains are generally spherical and measure about 25–50 micrometers in diameter, making the size and shape description correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Three of the four claims—those describing the bilobed dithecous tetragonal anther, the multinucleate nutritive tapetum, and the 25–50 micrometer spherical pollen grains—are correct, whereas the claim attributing microspore tetrad formation to mitosis is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q02 - Pollen wall composition, cellular shedding, and viability

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements about pollen grains in angiosperms:

Statement I: Sporopollenin in the exine can withstand high temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis, enabling pollen grains to be well-preserved as fossils.

Statement II: The intine is a thin, continuous inner layer composed of cellulose and pectin.

Statement III: In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 3-celled stage containing a vegetative cell and two male gametes.

Statement IV: Pollen grains of rice and wheat lose viability within 30 minutes of release, whereas pollen of many species can be stored for years in liquid nitrogen at \(-196^\circ\text{C}\).

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pollen grains represent the male gametophyte and possess a protective two-layered wall, defined cellularity at shedding, and species-specific viability durations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Exine and Intine
The hard outer exine is made of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known, which resists high temperatures, strong acids, alkalis, and known enzymes, allowing pollen grains to fossilise well. Beneath it, the inner intine is a thin and continuous layer made of cellulose and pectin. Both wall descriptions are therefore correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Shedding Stage and Viability
In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage (one vegetative cell and one generative cell), while in the remaining species the generative cell divides mitotically before shedding to form a 3-celled stage. Thus, claiming that over 60 per cent shed at the 3-celled stage is incorrect. Regarding viability, rice and wheat pollen lose viability within 30 minutes of release, and pollen grains of many species can be cryopreserved for years in liquid nitrogen at \(-196^\circ\text{C}\) in pollen banks, making the viability and storage claim correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Exactly three of the four claims—covering sporopollenin fossilisation, cellulose-pectin intine, and cereal viability versus liquid nitrogen storage—are correct, while the claim regarding the 3-celled shedding percentage is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q03 - Pistil, anatropous ovule, and embryo sac development

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the pistil, megasporangium, and female gametophyte:

Statement I: Papaver possesses a multicarpellary syncarpous pistil, whereas Michelia possesses a multicarpellary apocarpous gynoecium.

Statement II: In an ovule, the hilum represents the junction between the ovule and the funicle, and the chalaza represents the basal part opposite the micropylar end.

Statement III: Monosporic development of the embryo sac involves three sequential free-nuclear mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore nucleus.

Statement IV: A mature angiosperm embryo sac is 8-celled and 7-nucleate, with the filiform apparatus present at the chalazal end of the synergids.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The female reproductive structures include the pistil, the ovule (megasporangium), and the monosporic embryo sac formed by free-nuclear mitotic divisions of a single functional megaspore.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pistil and Ovule Structure
Papaver has fused carpels (multicarpellary syncarpous), while Michelia has free carpels (multicarpellary apocarpous). Inside the ovary, the ovule attaches to the placenta via the funicle, fusing at the hilum, with the chalaza located opposite the micropyle. Both the gynoecium comparison and the ovule anatomical descriptions are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Embryo Sac Development and Organisation
In monosporic development, the single functional megaspore nucleus undergoes three sequential free-nuclear mitotic divisions (2-nucleate, 4-nucleate, and 8-nucleate stages) without immediate cell wall formation, which is correct. After cellularisation, six nuclei form cells (three antipodals at the chalazal end, two synergids and one egg cell at the micropylar end) and two polar nuclei occupy the central cell, making the mature embryo sac 7-celled and 8-nucleate (not 8-celled and 7-nucleate). Moreover, the filiform apparatus is located at the micropylar tip of the synergids, not the chalazal end. Thus, the final description of the mature embryo sac is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding Papaver and Michelia gynoecia, hilum and chalaza positions, and three free-nuclear mitotic divisions are correct, whereas the claim calling the mature embryo sac 8-celled and 7-nucleate with a chalazal filiform apparatus is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q04 - Pollination types and abiotic versus biotic agents

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding pollination mechanisms and agents in angiosperms:

Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers in Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina remain closed, ensuring autogamy and assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators.

Statement II: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, yet genetically it is similar to autogamy.

Statement III: In water hyacinth and water lily, flowers emerge above the water surface and are pollinated by insects or wind rather than by water.

Statement IV: In Vallisneria, female flowers remain submerged and ribbon-like pollen grains are carried passively inside the water.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flowering plants exhibit autogamy, geitonogamy, and xenogamy, utilising abiotic (wind, water) and biotic (animal) agents with distinct floral adaptations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cleistogamy and Geitonogamy
Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina produce closed cleistogamous flowers where anthers and stigma lie close together, making them invariably autogamous with assured seed-set even without pollinators. Geitonogamy transfers pollen between different flowers of the same plant; thus it is functionally cross-pollination (requiring an agent) but genetically similar to autogamy. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Aquatic Pollination Modes
In emergent aquatic plants like water hyacinth and water lily, flowers rise above the water level and are pollinated by insects or wind, which is correct. However, in Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the surface of water via a long stalk and pollen is released onto the water surface, whereas submerged female flowers and ribbon-like pollen carried inside water are characteristic of marine seagrasses like Zostera. Therefore, attributing submerged pollination with ribbon-like pollen to Vallisneria is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding cleistogamy, geitonogamy, and emergent pollination in water hyacinth and water lily are correct, while the claim describing Vallisneria with submerged female flowers and ribbon-like pollen is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q05 - Outbreeding devices, pollen-pistil interaction, and hybridisation

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding outbreeding devices, pollen-pistil interaction, and artificial hybridisation:

Statement I: Monoecious plants such as castor and maize prevent autogamy but not geitonogamy, whereas dioecious plants such as papaya prevent both autogamy and geitonogamy.

Statement II: Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

Statement III: After reaching the ovary, the pollen tube enters the ovule through the chalaza and then enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus.

Statement IV: In artificial hybridisation, emasculation is required for bisexual female parent flowers before anther dehiscence, followed by bagging with butter paper.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Outbreeding devices discourage self-pollination, pollen-pistil interaction regulates compatible pollen tube entry into the ovule, and artificial hybridisation uses emasculation and bagging to ensure controlled crosses.

Step 2: Evaluation of Outbreeding Devices
Monoecious species (castor, maize) bear unisexual male and female flowers on the same plant, preventing autogamy while still allowing geitonogamy. Dioecious species (papaya) bear male and female flowers on separate plants, preventing both autogamy and geitonogamy. Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that inhibits germination or tube growth of self-pollen. Both claims are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Pollen Tube Entry and Artificial Hybridisation
After growing through the stigma and style to reach the ovary, the pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle—not the chalaza—and then enters one of the synergids guided by the filiform apparatus. Thus, stating that the pollen tube enters through the chalaza is incorrect. For artificial hybridisation, bisexual female flowers undergo emasculation (removal of anthers with forceps before dehiscence) and bagging (commonly with butter paper) to prevent unwanted pollen contamination, which is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding monoecy/dioecy, self-incompatibility, and emasculation/bagging are correct, whereas the claim that the pollen tube enters the ovule through the chalaza is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q06 - Double fertilisation events and post-fertilisation sequence

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding double fertilisation in angiosperms:

Statement I: The pollen tube discharges two male gametes into the cytoplasm of one of the synergids.

Statement II: Syngamy results in the formation of a diploid zygote by the fusion of one male gamete with the egg cell nucleus.

Statement III: Triple fusion results in the formation of a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) in the central cell.

Statement IV: After triple fusion, the central cell becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm, which precedes embryo development.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Double fertilisation is unique to angiosperms and involves two simultaneous fusion events—syngamy and triple fusion—that initiate embryo and endosperm formation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gamete Discharge and Syngamy
Upon entering a synergid via the filiform apparatus, the pollen tube releases two haploid male gametes into the synergid cytoplasm. One male gamete fuses with the haploid egg cell nucleus (syngamy) to form a diploid zygote. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Triple Fusion and Endosperm Initiation
The second haploid male gamete fuses with the two haploid polar nuclei in the central cell (triple fusion) to produce a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). The central cell then becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the nutritive endosperm, which precedes zygotic division and embryo development to ensure assured nutrition. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four claims accurately describe the events and sequence of double fertilisation and early post-fertilisation development.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q07 - Endosperm types, embryo anatomy, and perisperm

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding endosperm, embryo, and seed structure:

Statement I: In tender coconut, the coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm, while the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm.

Statement II: Pea and groundnut are non-albuminous seeds, whereas wheat, maize, barley, and castor are albuminous seeds.

Statement III: In grass embryos, the single lateral cotyledon is called the scutellum, and the shoot apex is enclosed in a hollow foliar structure called the coleorrhiza.

Statement IV: Persistent nucellus present in seeds of black pepper and beet is called perisperm.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Post-fertilisation development produces nutritive endosperm, a differentiated dicot or monocot embryo, and a mature seed that may retain endosperm or nucellus.

Step 2: Evaluation of Endosperm and Seed Types
In tender coconut, the liquid coconut water consists of thousands of free nuclei (free-nuclear endosperm), while the white kernel is cellular endosperm. Endosperm is completely consumed in non-albuminous seeds (pea, groundnut) and retained in albuminous seeds (wheat, maize, barley, castor). Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Grass Embryo and Perisperm
In grasses, the single lateral cotyledon is indeed the scutellum; however, the shoot apex and leaf primordia are enclosed in a hollow foliar structure called the coleoptile, whereas the coleorrhiza encloses the radicle and root cap. Thus, attributing shoot apex enclosure to the coleorrhiza is incorrect. Finally, residual persistent nucellus in black pepper and beet seeds is correctly termed perisperm.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding coconut endosperm, albuminous versus non-albuminous seeds, and perisperm in black pepper and beet are correct, while the claim assigning shoot apex enclosure to the coleorrhiza is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q08 - False fruits, parthenocarpy, seed longevity, apomixis, and polyembryony

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding fruits, seed viability, apomixis, and polyembryony:

Statement I: Apple, strawberry, and cashew are false fruits because the thalamus contributes to fruit formation.

Statement II: Parthenocarpic fruits such as banana develop without fertilisation and are seedless.

Statement III: Seeds of Lupinus arcticus from the Arctic Tundra remained viable for an estimated 10,000 years, and a 2,000-year-old viable seed of Phoenix dactylifera was discovered near the Dead Sea.

Statement IV: In many Citrus and Mango varieties, nucellar cells develop into embryos causing polyembryony, whereas apomixis in hybrid crops would prevent character segregation in progeny.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Angiosperm reproduction encompasses diverse fruit developmental pathways, remarkable seed dormancy records, and specialised asexual seed mechanisms like apomixis and polyembryony.

Step 2: Evaluation of False Fruits and Parthenocarpy
In apple, strawberry, and cashew, the thalamus contributes to fruit formation alongside the ovary, classifying them as false fruits. In banana, fruits develop without fertilisation (parthenocarpy) and are seedless. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Seed Longevity, Polyembryony, and Apomixis
Lupinus arcticus excavated from the Arctic Tundra germinated after an estimated 10,000 years of dormancy, and a 2,000-year-old viable seed of date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) was found at King Herod's palace near the Dead Sea. Additionally, nucellar cells protruding into the embryo sac produce multiple embryos (polyembryony) in many Citrus and Mango varieties, and making hybrid crops apomictic prevents segregation of hybrid characters in the progeny so farmers can reuse seeds year after year. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four claims accurately reflect the concepts of false fruits, parthenocarpy, seed viability records, nucellar polyembryony, and apomixis.
